changes: Place as_written extended to include the house reference 'etāgṛhā(va)sthita(?)' as transcribed
Notes expanded: śrī 3 Vajradevī is a deity, not a person; 'vajrā…' probably begins 'vajrācārya' before the scribe's name, but the name is lost; normalization to Kathmandu flagged as not fully certain

notes: The colophon breaks off on fol. 18r at 'vajrā…'. The cataloguer could not read the six lines on fol. 18v because the page is dark and the exposure blurred, so no scribe, donor or date survives in the transcription. 'vajrā…' probably begins the title vajrācārya (a priestly title) followed by the scribe's name, which is lost. 'śrī 3 vajradevīprasādena' invokes a deity's grace and does not name a person. Vasubandhu, Indrapṛṣṭa and the jinaśārdūla on fol. 9v are characters in the vratakathā, not people connected with this copy. talamuramahāvihāra = Tārumūla Mahāvihāra (catalogue: Taramula-Mahāvihāra). It is identified here as a vihāra in Kathmandu, but this identification is not fully certain. '(jontā)vāhāra' and 'khalucuka' are uncertain local names, probably a bāhāl and its courtyard (cuka/chowk).
